text:
The price was quite expensive.
But the male dentist who extracted the wisdom teeth was gentle and didn't hurt much. But the staff at the counter was terrible. I don't know what's wrong with them. Compared to other doctors who greeted me and smiled, the blonde, acne-prone staff at the counter was not very polite.
That day, I went for a consultation about tooth extraction and tooth extraction.
So, I asked a plump doctor or nurse about orthodontics. He showed me his mouth and teeth, gave me a brief introduction, and told me to come back another day.
But the staff at the counter interrupted me, saying I needed this kind of surgery.
In a few days, I was fine. My lower teeth were a bit protruding, but not too protruding, just my lower teeth overlapping my upper teeth.
But she said I needed jaw surgery. I was shocked, but I didn't say anything.
The next week, I was going to have another tooth extracted, but there was a long queue. I came back and tried consulting with a clinic near the Free Market. They gave excellent advice, saying my problem was just changing my tongue position because it was pushing against my lower teeth, and that I could get braces. That's all I had.
I don't plan on going to that clinic again because I'm so annoyed by the staff at the counter. If you don't know anything or truly have no knowledge, you shouldn't recommend or speak to patients or other clients in a way that would make them feel bad. Simply put, it's a disgrace that I'm not even a doctor.
The service was also poor. They didn't greet me or smile. I stood at the counter for a long time just to ask about the cost of braces. I stared and stared for a long time, and then I saw this shirt before I asked the nurse about braces.
I don't plan on going to this clinic again because I don't like the service of the staff at the counter.
